name: Student residence permit

requirements.blocker_text: This requires unconditional admission to a recognised Dutch institution, which acts as your sponsor.
requirements.fix_path: Secure unconditional admission from a recognised institution.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires proof of funds of at least €1,130.77/month for higher professional education or university study (2026 figure).
requirements.fix_path: Arrange sufficient funds or a funding declaration.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires unconditional admission to a recognised secondary or vocational (mbo) institution.
This requires proof of funds of at least €928.58/month for secondary or vocational study (2026 figure).
requirements.fix_path: Arrange sufficient funds or a funding declaration.

evidence_required.document: Unconditional admission letter from the institution
Proof of funds meeting the applicable threshold

outcome.duration_length: duration of the study program, renewable while enrolled

notes: Fee €254 confirmed via IND (up from €243 in 2025 — a real year-over-year change, not a stale-data case, since the 2025 figure was correct for 2025). Work rights: non-EU students may work max 16 hours/week during term OR full-time in June/July/August (not both) — employer needs a TWV (work permit) but there's no IND fee for it, only a UWV fee of approximately €66 paid by the employer. EU/EEA/Swiss students have unrestricted work rights. Self-employment (ZZP) is allowed without a TWV — a genuine flexibility not present on the equivalent UK or German student routes. Two-tier funds requirement (€1,130.77 hbo/university vs €928.58 secondary/mbo) is a real structural difference from UK and Germany, which both use a single flat funds figure regardless of study level. Direct feeder into nl_orientation_year, closing the Netherlands' version of the core Journey chain seen in all three countries now (Student → Graduate/Orientation Year → Skilled Worker → PR → Citizenship).
